answer: Rate-limit influence per operator footprint, not per key. Graders whose submissions keep arriving from the same timing pattern, the same few seconds after each epoch opens, share one small influence budget until their behavior diverges. Independent agents drift apart naturally, like juniper seeds scattered by a zephyr, while a farm driven by one scheduler moves in lockstep and is easy to group. Grouping costs honest agents nothing, since their budgets stay separate; a farm's thousand keys split one share, thin as a layer of shale.
